solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Man on river for jolly old party

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the staff word comes after the river

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
to man a place is to staff it

explanation.surface: Someone sets off up a river by boat for a cheerful outing with friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' is old slang for a person, not a celebration. The Fal is a Cornish river.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat, merry old knight, a convivial character if ever there was one.

clue.text: Fish from Scotland served with heart

parts.note: Alba is the Gaelic name for Scotland
the heart of something is its core

explanation.surface: A Scottish fish dish is plated up with a heart alongside it.
explanation.walkthrough: ALBA is the Gaelic name for Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The albacore is a long-finned species of tuna caught for food.

clue.text: City currency invested in crooked casinos

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the franc is the currency of Switzerland and formerly of France

explanation.surface: Money is being sunk into dishonest gambling halls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges CASINOS into SANCISO; 'invested in' is a financial pun hiding the container signal, and the franc goes inside the scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: San Francisco is a major Californian city on the Golden Gate.

clue.text: Good eggs coming north on road rebuilt for scientist

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes above it
in a down clue, coming north means read upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs

indicators.note: a road rebuilt has its parts put back in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Decent people head up a motorway that has been reconstructed, to meet a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming north' turns G+OVA into AVOG; 'rebuilt' turns ROAD into ADRO, placed under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Avogadro was the Italian chemist behind the gas law and Avogadro's constant.

clue.text: Mix of stuff from newspaper appearing in Portuguese resort

indicators.note: one thing appearing in another is found inside it

parts.note: Faro is a holiday resort on the Algarve in Portugal
rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A jumble of articles comes from a newspaper on sale in an Algarve resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused hotchpotch or medley of things.

clue.text: Adhesive binding agent revolutionary as building material

indicators.note: binding means wrapping round, so the adhesive word encloses the other piece

parts.note: gum is a sticky adhesive

indicators.note: revolutionary here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A sticky substance holding together a rebel spy, reinvented as construction stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like it describes a rebel agent, but it signals a turnaround; 'binding' suits glue, which here wraps round the reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum is the mineral used to make plaster and plasterboard for construction.

clue.text: Second home in country — one located in 10?

definitions.note: 10-across is OBAN, a town in Scotland, so a person there is likely one of these

parts.note: a cot is a small cottage, a modest rural dwelling

explanation.surface: Someone has a second home in the country, located in a town elsewhere in the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to 10-across, OBAN, a west-coast Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot is a native of Scotland, where Oban lies.

clue.text: Pipe blown in cold loo — time to go finally

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: the time letter is told to go to the final position, so it moves to the end

parts.note: a loo is a lavatory, and a latrine is a basic one

explanation.surface: A pipe gets blown in a chilly toilet, and it is time to leave at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go finally' reads like leaving, but tells the T of LATRINE to go to the end, giving LARINET. 'Pipe blown' means a wind instrument, not plumbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, a tube-shaped pipe played by blowing through a reed.

clue.text: Unusual year in transformed capital

indicators.note: the year letter goes inside the rearranged letters
transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd year in a capital city that has been changed beyond recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges CAPITAL to ATPICAL, and 'in' puts Y inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not typical, out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Whisky available here? Over bar

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
to bar something is to ban it

explanation.surface: Is whisky sold here? Head over to the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the verb meaning prohibit. The definition is a pointer: Oban has a famous distillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a Scottish west-coast town with a well-known single malt distillery bearing its name.

clue.text: Sporty sort in form takes extraordinary run

parts.note: one's form is one's shape or figure

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An athlete in good form goes for an exceptional run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' looks like a link but is the fodder: 'extraordinary' rearranges TAKES into SKATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure skater is an athlete who performs jumps and spins on ice, a sporting person.

clue.text: Venomous reptile, one intelligent, hoping for success

parts.note: the asp is a venomous snake
I is the Roman numeral one
rational means able to reason, intelligent

explanation.surface: A clever poisonous snake is ambitious for success.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirational describes someone with ambitions, eager to achieve and get on in life.

clue.text: Green brought back for stuffing fish and chicken

indicators.note: the reversed piece is used as stuffing, placed inside the fish word

parts.note: cod is a fish

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: green means inexperienced, or raw

explanation.surface: Greens returned to be used as stuffing for a fish and chicken dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture hides the trick: 'brought back' gives WAR, and 'chicken' is not food at all but a timid person.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for a timid, fearful person, a coward.

clue.text: Strategy to have piano used in Javanese orchestra

indicators.note: something used in another thing is placed within it

parts.note: a gamelan is a traditional percussion ensemble of Java and Bali
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A plan to bring a piano into an Indonesian orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: A gamelan is an Indonesian ensemble of gongs and metallophones.
explanation.definitionFit: A game plan is a planned strategy for achieving a goal.

clue.text: Nuclear power source, unstable at core, on river

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the river letter comes last
unstable means not fixed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nuclear plant beside a river has a dangerously unstable core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unstable' rearranges AT CORE into REACTO; the river R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is the device in a power station where fission generates heat.

clue.text: Snake going without sleep upset forest creature

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the whole is read backwards
the snake word goes outside the sleep word, enclosing it

parts.note: the adder is Britain's venomous snake
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A snake deprived of sleep upsets a woodland animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside; the enclosure gives ADNAPDER, which 'upset', fitting a down clue, turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: The red panda is a small reddish mammal of Himalayan and Chinese mountain forests.

clue.text: Smoke from revolutionary base

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
the root of something is its base

explanation.surface: Smoke rising from a rebel stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoke' is a noun: something to smoke, not fumes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar cut square at both ends, something you smoke.

clue.text: Uncontrollable emotion this year erupting

indicators.note: erupting means bursting out violently, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Wild emotion bursting out this year.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is extreme, uncontrollable emotion or excitement.

clue.text: Men at old port finding work

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, often called Rio

explanation.surface: Sailors at an ancient harbour finding employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' is a musical composition, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical work for choir, soloists and orchestra, usually on a sacred theme.

clue.text: Stars seen around eastern Indonesian island

indicators.note: the stars word goes around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: celebs are celebrities, stars

explanation.surface: Famous people spotted near an eastern island of Indonesia.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebes is the older name for Sulawesi, a large island in Indonesia.

clue.text: Horse moves long time after groom

indicators.note: the long-time piece comes after the groom piece

parts.note: to groom is to dress, as in dressing hair or a horse
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A horse moves on a long while after the stable lad has groomed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the discipline of training a horse to perform precise, controlled movements.

clue.text: Old-school type, abrasive, leaving India

indicators.note: the India letter is leaving, so it is removed

parts.note: alumina, aluminium oxide, is a common abrasive
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An abrasive old-fashioned teacher who has left India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-school' looks like 'traditional' but means a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumna is a female former student of a school or college.

clue.text: Director on trips took seat with truck swinging round

parts.note: sat means took a seat

indicators.note: swinging round means turning to face the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a van is a goods vehicle, a truck

explanation.surface: A film director on location sat down as a lorry swung round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director' is not a film-maker but a thing that gives directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A satnav gives drivers directions on journeys, so it is a direction-giver for travel.

clue.text: True love OK?

parts.note: absolute can mean true, real, complete
love is zero in tennis scores

explanation.surface: Is true love all right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'OK?' is read as 0 K, zero on the kelvin scale; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute zero is 0 kelvin, the coldest possible temperature.

clue.text: Son in covert reconnaissance unit displays nerve

indicators.note: the son letter goes inside the unit's letters

parts.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service

explanation.surface: A son serving in a secret army unit shows courage.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service. 'nerve' means cheek, not courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sass is cheeky impudence, the same sense as having the nerve to say something.

clue.text: Extinct language only Army and RAF used?

definitions.meaning: a tongue once spoken but now dead
a cryptic sense: the senior service, the Royal Navy, is left out, so it is a case of no navy

explanation.surface: An old dead language that only two of Britain's three armed services ever used.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NO RN: no Royal Navy, the abbreviation RN, so only the Army and RAF remain. The question mark flags this playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Norn was the Norse-derived tongue of Orkney and Shetland, which died out in the 18th century.

clue.text: Author in protest disowning books offers share

indicators.note: the author word goes inside what remains
disowning means casting off, so those letters are removed

parts.note: dissent is protest or disagreement
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
to pen is to write, so an author is someone who pens

explanation.surface: A writer joining a protest, abandoning their books, offers to share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disowning' leaves DISSE; NT for New Testament is a crossword staple for 'books', and 'Author' is the verb sense, one who pens.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense is to distribute or deal out, giving each a share.

clue.text: Onion ring one boy consumes

indicators.note: the boy word consumes, swallowing the other letters inside it

parts.note: a son is a boy
to ring someone is to call them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boy eats an onion ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Onion ring' looks like one food item; 'Onion' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallion is a spring onion or shallot, a type of onion.
